sources.entry: Scaled Dot-Product Attention (oneDNN Graph) - Fixes the fused attention pattern, f32 accumulation under bf16 inputs and the shapes the fast CPU path accepts.

summary.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention (SDPA)
summary.one_liner: oneDNN's guide to the floating-point SDPA graph pattern (MatMul, Scale, Mask, SoftMax, MatMul), its f32-intermediate data type rules, and the CPU and GPU shapes that get the optimized path.
takeaways: SDPA is defined as a DAG of MatMul, optional Scale, optional Mask, SoftMax, optional Dropout, and a second MatMul, with optional Reorder at the end.
With bf16 or f16 Q/K/V, the first MatMul output, Scale, Mask and SoftMax input stay in f32 intermediates.
On CPU, the optimized inference path requires 4D Q/K shaped (N, H, S, D_qk) and V shaped (N, H, S, D_v), and for OpenMP needs N * H > 2 * thread count.
The reference implementation stores the Query-Key dot products, which takes O(S^2) memory and can run out of memory for long sequences.
Masks can be explicit (Add with -inf, or boolean Select) or implicit (causal mask built from GenIndex, Add, Subtract, GreaterEqual, Select).
summary.summary: The page is the oneDNN developer guide section on Scaled Dot-Product Attention. It defines the floating-point SDPA graph for inference, training forward and training backpropagation, listing each operation (MatMul, Scale, Mask, SoftMax, Dropout, Reorder) and which are required or optional. It then explains the f32 intermediate data type rules for bf16 and f16 inputs, the implementation limits, and the CPU and GPU input shapes that have optimized implementations. It closes with pointers to SDPA, MQA and implicit causal mask examples.
